title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Fever and chills

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 78, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 99.1 F

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fever, chills, malaise.
Respiratory: Negative for cough, shortness of breath.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain, palpitations.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea, diarrhea.
Genitourinary: Negative for dysuria.

History of Present Illness: (Copied Forward) Patient is a 78-year-old male presenting with a three-day history of subjective fevers and associated rigors. He reports generalized fatigue but denies any significant shortness of breath or localized pain.

Hospital Course: The patient was admitted for evaluation of a persistent fever. Blood cultures were obtained upon arrival. Results confirmed the presence of bacteremia. Clinical assessment indicates that the patient does not have sepsis. He remained stable throughout the stay and was transitioned to oral antibiotics for continued management of the bacteremia. He tolerated the transition well and was cleared for discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses: 
1. Bacteremia
2. Fever

Discharge Medications:
- Amoxicillin 875mg TID
- Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for fever

Follow-up: Follow up with primary care physician in 7 days.

Electronically signed, 
R. Mensah, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Bacteremia without sepsis is coded R78.81 (no HCC), which is not a sepsis code: no sepsis code applies.

distractors.why: The provider documents bacteremia without sepsis.
